caption: Massive volume, into one defined stage. Sales works what lands there.

customers-do-not-arrive-alone.description: "You can't wait for users to come to you. You have to go out and get them": getting users is a gradual process, and early numbers look too small only to those who underestimate compound growth.[1]

graham-do-things-that-dont-scale.title: Paul Graham, Do Things that Don't Scale

the-marketing-hand-off-has-its-own-rate.header: The marketing hand-off has its own rate
the-marketing-hand-off-has-its-own-rate.description: In one vendor dataset the rate from marketing-qualified to sales-qualified lead was 68 percent, against a 19 percent win rate further down; stage rates are measured on one company's own stage definitions.[1]

ebsta-gtm-benchmarks.title: Ebsta and Pavilion, GTM Benchmarks Report

two-ways-in.title: Two ways in
two-ways-in.script: There are two ways to get a lead. You go and get it, or it walks in on its own, and marketing is the second way.

volume-into-a-defined-stage.title: Volume into a defined stage
volume-into-a-defined-stage.script: Marketing speaks to many people at once, so that a customer enters themselves into a defined stage. An inbound lead is one example, an e-commerce checkout is another.

hand-to-sales.title: Hand to sales
hand-to-sales.script: Marketing fills the stage and sales works what lands in it. Which means marketing does not replace the first call, it gives that call someone to be made to.
